speaker: Doctor
text: The blood work will be crucial, but have you noticed any skin changes like jaundice or easy bruising, or any history of liver disease? REQUEST TEST: Liver_Function_Panel, Bilirubin, Alkaline_Phosphatase.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the liver panel results; since those are normal, have you noticed any difficulty swallowing solids or liquids, or any visible lumps in your neck other than the supraclavicular node?

Also, have you recently been exposed to anyone diagnosed with tuberculosis or HIV, or do you have a history of smoking?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CTA, Neck_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The swelling being "fixed" and painless is highly concerning for malignancy. Have you noticed any blood in your stool, or have you had unintentional weight loss beyond the 12 pounds you already mentioned?

REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Occult_Blood, CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fecal_Occult_Blood: NORMAL READINGS; CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis: Massively enlarged axillary, mediastinal, and cervical lymph nodes

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Hodgkin Lymphoma or Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma).

The combination of B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), a fixed painless supraclavicular node, and massively enlarged lymph nodes in the axilla, mediastinum, and cervical regions on the CT scan is highly characteristic of lymphoma. Do you have a history of previous autoimmune disorders or a family history of lymphatic cancers?
